adds.title: LGBTQ rights in Turkey - Wikipedia
adds.summary: Wikipedia's national 'LGBTQ rights in Turkey' page documents the framework a trans visitor to Siirt stands under: homosexuality was decriminalised in 1858 under the Ottoman penal code and legal gender change has been possible since 1988, but same-sex marriage is not recognised and LGBTQ people are barred from serving openly in the military. Pride events have been repeatedly blocked by governors — the 2015-2018 Istanbul parades were banned by local authorities, and on 14 June 2019 the Istanbul, İzmir and Antalya prides were all banned by the cities' governors. The page records a proposal to criminalize publicly encouraging 'behavior contrary to biological sex' with a one-to-three-year prison sentence, which was ultimately not included in the 12th judicial package (omnibus bill). This provincial record makes no Siirt-specific claim; the page supports the record's national-framework claims, which is the only documented basis.

adds.title: Human rights in Türkiye - Amnesty International (Report 2025/26)
adds.summary: Amnesty's Türkiye country report (Report 2025/26) records the national framework governing a visitor to Siirt: in June 2025 blanket bans were issued against the Istanbul LGBTI and Trans pride marches, police subjected peaceful protesters to unlawful force, over 90 people were arbitrarily detained, and prosecutions of 92 people for participating in pride marches continued at year's end. In December 2025 an İzmir court ordered the dissolution of the Young LGBTI+ Association, ruling it had shared 'obscene' images incompatible with 'society's moral values'. The report also records that three draft law packages targeting LGBTI people were made public in 2025 — criminalizing LGBTI identity expression and consensual same-sex relations and making legal gender recognition nearly impossible — though they were ultimately not submitted to parliament. No Siirt-specific incident is documented; this is the province-level applicable national framework.
